title: What does happiness mean to you?
subtitle: An imaginary Partner Day for Example Homes. A preview of listening with dembrane.
disclosure: All statements, tensions and perspectives in this example were invented for demonstration purposes. This is not a report of the Partner Day and does not show what people actually think.
invitation_text:
The real stories come from your partners.

We look forward to listening to your partners together. Their experiences, questions and differences give happiness its meaning. That is how we make the day worthwhile and fill this screen with real stories and perspectives.
notice: Synthetic demo · invented perspectives, not real conversation outcomes.

conversations.label: Table 1 · A secure home
conversations.transcript:
SYNTHETIC DEMO. A wholly invented conversation. No statements by real people.

Fictional voice 1: Happiness starts when you can catch your breath at home.
Fictional voice 2: An affordable rent gives you room in your head.
Fictional voice 3: Sustainable housing has to be affordable today as well.
Fictional voice 1: A repair is only finished when the tenant can get on with life.
Fictional voice 2: People with little room cannot wait for later.
Fictional voice 3: How do we notice that a house really becomes a home?

tensions.knot: Making homes sustainable prepares them for later, but people who are short now cannot carry tomorrow's costs today.
tensions.toResolve: How do we discuss housing costs and future-proofing in one conversation, without one pushing the other aside?

tensions.poleB: Quiet and a space of your own
tensions.knot: A hello and a community room bring people together, but those looking for quiet feel shut out rather than welcome in a busy activity.
tensions.toResolve: How does meeting happen without joining in becoming an obligation?

tensions.knot: People with little room want to know now where they stand; people who think along drop out when the choice turns out to be made already.
tensions.toResolve: Which choices are still really open, and do we say so up front?

tensions.knot: A goal helps to follow what changes, but happiness cannot be filled in for someone else or caught in one number.
tensions.toResolve: Which signals do tenants choose themselves, and which story belongs with each number?

stakeholders.name: Tenants
stakeholders.role: Tenants of Example Homes, talked about at every table.
stakeholders.stake: An affordable, safe home, and noticing that their story changes something.

stakeholders.name: Households short of space
stakeholders.role: Tenants and home seekers for whom waiting is not an option.
stakeholders.stake: Clarity now about what is possible.

stakeholders.name: Neighbourhood partners
stakeholders.role: Those who keep meeting places and community rooms open.
stakeholders.stake: Places where people feel welcome, also without joining in.

stakeholders.name: Example Homes staff
stakeholders.role: At the table about their own work, the handover and their happiness at work.
stakeholders.stake: Time and room to listen, ask difficult questions and solve things together.

stakeholders.name: Care and welfare partners
stakeholders.role: Organisations a tenant's question goes to or falls between.
stakeholders.stake: A warm handover and someone who stays involved.

stakeholders.name: Quiet voices
stakeholders.role: Tenants who do not join in by themselves or are not at the table yet.
stakeholders.stake: Being heard without joining in becoming a hurdle.

relations.label: being heard
relations.detail: Tenants want to notice what happens with their story; thinking along feels different when the choice is already fixed.

aspects.note: Whether tenants really have influence depends on what is still open up front.
